title: Span-aligned kernel cost and attention-path tracing
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Goal: produce low-overhead, actionable traces that correlate host-level request spans (OpenTelemetry) with device-level kernel execution so we can: 1) attribute GPU cost to logical stages (prefill vs decode, attention vs FFN), 2) trace attention-path variants across layers and runtime kernel implementations, and 3) power optimizations (kernel selector rules) with per-request signals. This ticket implements span-aligned NVTX range conventions, a device->host correlation token, and a sampling strategy for production telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: Instrumented prefill and decode paths emit NVTX ranges and a correlation token that can be mapped to host OpenTelemetry spans in the existing tracing pipeline.
Grafana dashboard shows per-kernel GPU time, count, and average enqueue-to-complete latency broken down by logical stage (prefill/decode/attention/ffn) for a sample workload.
End-to-end attribution: for a 8k token synthetic workload, per-kernel time attribution sums to >=95% of observed GPU busy time in a fully instrumented run.
Production overhead when sampling at 1% is <2% tail latency increase and <1% CPU overhead in workload tests.
Kernel metadata includes: impl name, quantization profile, batch-size hint, and a short 12-char signature token to match across traces and device metrics.
Documentation and a Confluence design doc with naming conventions and examples are published and linked from this ticket.
One smoke PR merged that adds a minimal opt-in env var to enable the new naming and correlation in CI/preview builds.
A follow-up task is created if any GPU vendor requires additional hooks (CUPTI/roctracer) for accurate timing on their stacks.
progress_updates: 2026-02-28: Kickoff meeting with runtime, infra-tracing, and observability. Agreed on goals and success criteria.
2026-03-02: PoC NVTX naming scheme implemented in a local build. Example range format: rtd:pf:attn:L{layer}:impl={impl}:sig={token}. Confirmed ranges are visible in local Nsight and perf traces.
2026-03-04: Implemented host-side correlation token propagation. Host span attaches attribute 'rtd.sig' which matches NVTX 'sig' tag on device ranges.
2026-03-07: Added per-kernel metrics emission (prometheus histograms) for enqueue->complete latency and kernel duration. Initial numbers look plausible on 8xA100 test rig.
2026-03-09: End-to-end trace example created and uploaded to Confluence (link below). Noted a 7% overhead in full-instrumentation mode; will rely on sampling for production.
2026-03-10: PR opened with feature gated behind REDWOOD_RUNTIME_TRACE=1. Requesting review from @Marissa (observability) and @Raj (runtime).
decisions: Adopt NVTX range naming convention that includes logical stage + layer + impl + short signature to make search and grouping easy in traces.

Use a 12-character signature token computed from kernel parameters (kernel name, grid/block dims, quantization flag, common launch args) hashed with BLAKE2s and truncated — chosen for stability and small footprint.
Sampling approach: 1% random sampling in production, plus deterministic capture for p99 requests (trigger when host span duration > release-specific threshold).
Emit per-kernel Prometheus metrics (counters/histograms) labeled by stage and impl alongside trace NVTX ranges to support both high-cardinality and aggregated dashboards.
Do not enable full CUPTI-based capture by default due to complexity and perf risk; add a vendor-integration subtask for deeper timing if needed.
Keep the feature behind an opt-in env var for initial rollout and add a feature flag for customer enablement in Dedicated/Private environments.
Kernel selector will start recording the chosen impl label into the span so rollout regressions can be detected via existing alerting (quality/regression hooks will be added in a follow-up).
risks: Full instrumentation significantly increases latency and GPU-side overhead; mitigated by sampling and opt-in gating.

Different GPU vendors expose timing differently (CUPTI vs roctracer); risk of inconsistent metrics across regions. We will detect and name vendor-specific gaps in telemetry and create vendor sub-tasks.
High-cardinality labels (layer + impl + sig) could increase ingestion costs in metrics backend; we will limit cardinality in production metrics and send full labels only in sampled traces.
Correlation token collision risk is low but nonzero for truncated tokens. Collision rate will be monitored and token length increased if necessary.
Security: avoid embedding PII in kernel names or traces. Reviewed by Security during rollout planning.
next_steps: Complete PR reviews and merge runtime + observability changes (owners: Leo, Marissa).
Run load tests with 0.5%, 1%, and 5% sampling on staging clusters and capture latency/CPU/GPU overhead matrices (owner: Raj).
Create a lightweight CI smoke test that validates correlation tokens are present in both host spans and NVTX ranges (owner: Sofia).
Publish a short runbook for on-call explaining how to interpret the new dashboard and how to temporarily disable tracing if we see regressions (owner: Marissa).
If staging results are acceptable, start a canary rollout in a small Dedicated pool with the env var enabled for a single customer-internal team. Collect feedback and iterate.
